extracted.intended_audience: news editors, journalists, media critics, and engaged news readers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for selecting and ordering stories on a mainstream news homepage (what belongs above the fold and what should be demoted). Normative rubric aimed at improving civic utility of homepage journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threats to democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-democratic actions by elected officials, especially patterns rather than one-offs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize reporting that documents actions undermining democratic norms and institutions; focus on recurring behavior and institutional impact rather than isolated incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct quotes revealing intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct quotes from the powerful that reveal intent (not laundered through 'sources say').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer on-the-record statements that show motive or intent; avoid relying on anonymous, secondhand attributions that obscure responsibility and meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy consequences for ordinary people
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy consequences for ordinary people (not Beltway insider reaction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize how policies affect everyday lives rather than centering elite reaction or insider political calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypocrisy or contradiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Hypocrisy / contradiction between stated principle and action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight clear mismatches between public claims and actual behavior or policy; show how rhetoric diverges from practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern recognition / connective context
rubrics_metrics.description: Pattern recognition — connect today's story to last week's, last year's.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualize individual stories within larger patterns over time to reveal systemic issues rather than treating events in isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid elevating horse-race polling
rubrics_metrics.description: Horse-race polling at expense of stakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not prioritize or lead with polling numbers when they distract from the substantive stakes or impacts of a story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid false equivalence / both-sides framing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist framing that presents unequal actors, facts, or moral positions as equivalent; make asymmetry clear in placement and headlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid process-over-substance coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Process stories (who's up / down) over substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't let internal political maneuvering or personnel gossip dominate top-of-homepage placement when substantive policy or public-impact reporting is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: De-prioritize personality and access journalism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit elevation of celebrity, personality-driven pieces, or access-focused scoops that do not materially inform civic decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid anonymous-source spin
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be skeptical of anonymous attributions that advance partisan spin; require corroboration and avoid letting operatives' narratives drive the homepage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't stenograph official statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Stenography of official statements without fact-check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reproducing official statements verbatim as lead copy; fact-check, challenge claims, and provide necessary context before elevating them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civic utility test for placement
rubrics_metrics.description: "Does this story leave the reader better able to act as a citizen?" — if not, it doesn't belong on A1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use civic utility as a primary criterion for above-the-fold placement: prioritize stories that inform voters' or citizens' understanding and capacity to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede must not bury the lede
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories where the lede buries the lede.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frontload the essential facts and implications; avoid narratives that hide the main point deep in the copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headlines should not euphemize
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear, direct headlines that accurately convey severity or wrongdoing rather than softening language that reduces perceived importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat lying as fact when warranted
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage that treats lying as an interesting strategic choice rather than a fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report false statements as factual falsehoods when evidence shows they are untrue; do not frame lies solely as strategy or entertaining behavior.
